answer: CORROBORATED. The upstream carries dense, gap-free store-level history across the whole b1..b4 span, and 421 stores trade on every one of its 24 days -- against an independently projected h28 of 419.
consequence: The last untested assumption on the b3 critical path is retired. Queue s4,b1,b2,b3,b4,s5 stands unchanged; no rescope, no reorder, no additional slice is indicated by this measurement.

findings.finding: No gap day exists. All 24 days of 2026-04-29..2026-05-22 carry 497-527 transacting stores (median 513); zero sparse days, zero empty days. Nothing inside the backwards span can break the 28-consecutive-prior-day requirement.

Early-May store density runs at 0.9344 of the landed control fortnight (median 513 vs 549 stores/day) -- a smooth secular growth trend, not a cliff. The donated store set is therefore modestly generous, so realised h28 should land slightly under 419, with margin that dwarfs criterion 3's requirement.

421 stores trade on every one of the 24 backwards days. The critical-path projection reached 419 by an independent route (landed PG streaks plus donation). Two independent methods converging on ~420 corroborate the plan; neither is now the sole support for criterion 3.

Scope limit: this measures the upstream pre-image of a transacting store-day, not landed rows. It cannot predict per-store mapping attrition, and it is not a substitute for the post-activation verify -- it retires the assumption, not the acceptance evidence.

measurements.grain: distinct place per createdAt UTC day, state=TRADE_SUCCESS and currency=TWD

method.control_rationale: Unmapped places quarantine, so upstream distinct-place counts are an UPPER BOUND on landed stores. A landed control fortnight measured the identical way cancels that bias; the claim is relative density, not absolute.
method.disturbance: 64Mi/10m request on private-pool, which sat at 96% memory with slice -s4 mid-flight; probe completed in ~20s, s4 pod unbroken at RESTARTS 0.
method.faithfulness: Grain taken from scripts/models/sql/model_ready_views.sql (transaction_source filters transaction_status='succeeded' AND currency='TWD'; transaction_daily groups by (event_time AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::date) and from apps/data_platform/mapping.py::project_transaction (event_time=createdAt, succeeded=state TRADE_SUCCESS, currency=`currency or payment.currency` uppercased, store identity = place -> place.store_id).
method.grain: distinct place per createdAt UTC day, state=TRADE_SUCCESS and currency=TWD
method.plane: SOURCE MongoDB Atlas fongniao_prod.orders, read-only aggregation

question: horizon_critical_path.json projects b1..b3 move h28 from 0 to 419 by DONATING a landed dense-day store set to each backwards date. That donation had never been checked against the source. Order-count depth (probe P4) does not answer it: 11k orders can come from 200 stores or 600, and a single gap day inside the window breaks every store's consecutive run.
